question: Can the blocking 16-20 ms/step D2H readback at _read_sample be deferred or overlapped to recover decode-step wall time?
answer: No. The readback waits on GPU work that must happen anyway, so the time is GPU-busy rather than GPU-idle, and the dependency (sampled token -> next step's embedding gather) is strict.

method.phase_split_source: child-only run, no profiler: each measured step wall is split into the blocking readback inside _read_sample and host time outside it, attributed by wrapping runtime.memcpy and snapshotting per-call-site totals around each step
method.overlap_source: the committed P5 attribution artifact's api_while_gpu_idle_ns, which bounds how much of ANY HIP API time can be GPU-idle time
method.why_two_sources: the phase split alone cannot say whether the blocked host time is wasted; pairing it with the traced GPU-idle split is what decides the question

gpu_idle_bound.derivation: at most api_while_gpu_idle_ms_per_step of ALL HIP API time in a step can be GPU-idle, and the readback is one HIP API call, so at least (readback - api_while_gpu_idle) of the readback overlaps GPU-busy time

conclusion.strict_dependency: the sampled token index is read back to the host, which then builds the next step's input embedding (_copy_token_embeddings_to_device); the host cannot enqueue the next step without it
conclusion.real_bottleneck: host-side launch and Python work: the GPU is idle about 19.3 ms/step while the host enqueues ~793 kernel launches/step and spends ~14.95 ms/step outside the readback
conclusion.redirect: reduce launch count or amortize it (graph capture already exists on the c8 packed route with one replay per logical transition), rather than deferring the readback

limits: The phase split is from a child-only run and is not itself profiled, so it does not independently confirm that the GPU is busy during the readback; that rests on the committed trace's api_while_gpu_idle_ns, which bounds all HIP API time rather than the readback alone.

The two runs differ: the phase split measured a 35.079 ms median step and a 20.186 ms median readback, while the committed attribution measured 36.605 ms and 16.296 ms. The overlap conclusion holds in both, but the absolute split is not identical across runs.
The 14.95 ms/step of host-outside-readback time is not decomposed into launch overhead versus Python bookkeeping; naming that split is the next measurement.
No optimization was attempted, so this is a negative result about the readback hypothesis, not a measurement of any launch-reduction alternative.
notes: performance_claim is false and no scoreboard row changed: this redirects an optimization target rather than reporting a speedup.
Follow-up task #23 asked for exactly this fork: either a gated win or a recorded negative result naming the dependency that makes the time unhideable.
